title: In Lazio, a Week-Long Climb at the Pump — But Still Cheaper Than the Rest of Italy
dek: Seven straight days of rising gasoline and diesel prices haven't pushed Lazio above the national average — yet.
body: Drivers filling up self-service in Lazio paid €1.985 per liter for Benzina and €2.183 for Gasolio as of July 28 — both a shade below Italy's national self-service averages of €1.998 and €2.200. That gap, about 1.3 cents on gasoline and 1.7 cents on diesel, keeps the region among the more affordable stops on the map, even as prices have been anything but flat.

The trend is unmistakably upward: Benzina has risen every single day this week, climbing from €1.945 on July 21 to today's €1.985 — a nearly 4-cent increase in seven days. Gasolio moved even further, up almost 7 cents over the same stretch, though it eased slightly on the most recent day. Meanwhile Lazio's station network held steady, with 2,361 registered stations and 2,105 reporting prices today (about 89%), a sign the local retail network remains active and largely unchanged week to week.

Numbers like these — drilled down to a single region, tracked day over day — are only practical because this dashboard rebuilds itself automatically every morning, with no manual spreadsheet involved. Built with Claude Code, the pipeline pulls the latest MIMIT data, recomputes every region and comune, and republishes the site without a person touching a formula. That's what makes a spotlight like Lazio's possible on an ordinary Wednesday, not just at the end of the month.
pull_quote: Lazio's diesel prices climbed nearly 7 cents in a week — yet still undercut the rest of Italy by almost 2 cents a liter.
